H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H3467: properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H1584: to end (in the sense of completion or failure)
H539: properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain;
H1121: a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.)
H120: ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.)
H7723: evil (as destructive), literally (ruin) or morally (especially guile); figuratively idolatry (as false, subjective), uselessness (as deceptive, objective; also adverbially, in vain)
H1696: perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue
H376: a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
H854: properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc.
H8193: the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.)
H2513: properly, smoothness; figuratively, flattery; also an allotment
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
H3772: to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces)
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H3956: the tongue (of man or animals), used literally (as the instrument of licking, eating, or speech), and figuratively (speech, an ingot, a fork of flame, a cove of water)
H1419: great (in any sense); hence, older; also insolent
H834: who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc.
H1396: to be strong; by implication, to prevail, act insolently
H4310: who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix
H6258: at this time, whether adverb, conjunction or expletive
H6965: to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)
H7896: to place (in a very wide application)
H6315: to puff, i.e. blow with the breath or air; hence, to fan (as a breeze), to utter, to kindle (a fire), to scoff
H2889: pure (in a physical, chemical, ceremonial or moral sense)
H3701: silver (from its pale color); by implication, money
H6884: to fuse (metal), i.e. refine (literally or figuratively)
H5948: probably a crucible (as working over the metal)
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H8104: properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc.
H5341: to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.)
H4480: properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses
H1755: properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling
H5769: properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always
H5439: (as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around
H7563: morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
H1980: to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
H7311: to be high actively, to rise or raise (in various applications, literally or figuratively)
H2149: properly, a shaking, i.e. perhaps a tempest
